2	// a dark_oak dressing table with a stool and a standing lantern, a barrel dresser, a white carpet rug, hanging lanterns).
3	// Inner air x65..68, z43..49, y11..16. Doorways: west x64 z46..47 (from the master bedroom), south x66..67 z50 (from the
4	// east upper corridor). Lanes kept clear: x65 z46..47 and x66..67 z49 (plus x67 z48 to link them).
5	import { layers } from "/Volumes/ext1/swe/repos/minecraft-design/tools/src/build.mjs";
6	
7	// HELD: parts/shell.mjs carves the whole interior to air, and runParts locks every cell an earlier part placed (air
8	// included), so every write below is refused. The layout stays here as data; the layers() call is off until the shell
9	// stops claiming the room's air.
10	export function build(g) {
11	  const origin = [65, 11, 43];
12	  const legend = {
13	    C: ["cauldron", { level: "0" }], // basin, by the north window
14	    T: ["water_cauldron", { level: "3" }], // the tub, along the east wall (focal piece, seen from the west door)
15	    F: "dark_oak_fence", // dressing-table post
16	    t: ["dark_oak_slab", { type: "top" }], // dressing-table top
17	    s: ["dark_oak_stairs", { facing: "east", half: "bottom", shape: "straight" }], // stool, back to the east
18	    B: "barrel", // linen dresser
19	    W: "white_carpet", // rug between the tub and the doors
20	    L: ["lantern", { hanging: "false" }], // standing lantern on the table top
21	    h: ["lantern", { hanging: "true" }], // hanging lanterns from the ceiling
22	  };
23	  const blank = ["    ", "    ", "    ", "    ", "    ", "    ", "    "];
24	  const rows = (...r) => r;
25	  const layersByY = [
26	    // y11: floor furniture (rows z43..49, columns x65..68)
27	    rows(
28	      "C   ", // z43 basin
29	      "   T", // z44 tub
30	      "   T", // z45 tub
31	      " WW ", // z46 rug (x65 kept clear for the west door)
32	      " WW ", // z47 rug
33	      "Fs B", // z48 table, stool, barrel
34	      "B  B", // z49 barrels (x66..67 kept clear for the south door)
35	    ),
36	    // y12: table top slab
37	    rows("    ", "    ", "    ", "    ", "    ", "t   ", "    "),
38	    // y13: lantern on the table
39	    rows("    ", "    ", "    ", "    ", "    ", "L   ", "    "),
40	    blank, // y14
41	    blank, // y15
42	    // y16: hanging lanterns under the ceiling
43	    rows("  h ", "    ", " h  ", "    ", "    ", "  h ", "    "),
44	  ];
45	  // layers(g, origin, legend, layersByY) would place the layout; refused by the shell's air lock, so nothing is written.
46	  void origin; void legend; void layersByY;
47	  return { placed: 0 };
48	}
49

content.text: The lock refused the lamp, so the built bath still has its dark corner. I'm stopping on this part: the fix is in the shell and the shared build library, not in files I'm allowed to touch. I'll report that through the structured output.

input.summary:
Master bath: one standing lantern at (65,11,45) gives min 8 and no dim cell on a scratch copy (room-15.mjs carries it at the end of build(g)). The lamp is refused in build.nbt by the shell's air lock, so the built bath still reads min 0 with 1 dark cell at (68,11,49).
The designer's three hanging lanterns alone give min 7 (3 dim cells), so the plan's hanging points do not reach the 8 bar on their own.
Not finished: the lamp needs the shell to stop claiming the bath's air, or the lock to let room parts write into air.
left: build.nbt has no bath lamp: parts-report says 'room: master bath' refused 1 at (65,11,45) lantern over air. The bath is min 0 with 1 dark cell (68,11,49) until that is fixed.

Root cause is upstream: parts/shell.mjs writes air over the whole bath interior (owned by the shell), and runParts' lock refuses every later write into an owned cell, air included. Every room module is HELD for this reason (room-15 places 0 blocks, furniture too). Fix is either shell.mjs stops claiming room air, or the shared build.mjs lock lets room parts write into air a part placed. Neither file is mine to change.

Scratch measurements, not in build.nbt (scratch files in /tmp/lamp-scratch): hanging lanterns at (67,16,43), (66,16,45), (67,16,48) alone give min 7 with 3 dim cells; plus the table lantern at (65,13,48) (with fence and top slab) gives min 8 but mcd walk then reports NEEDS WORK over an unreached cell at (65,14,48) on top of that lantern. The lamplighter chose the single floor lantern (min 8, 0 dim, walk OK 28/28).

Designer's ask was to check the bath light once the house is built. Ceiling y17 at the hanging points is white_concrete and the floor is oak_planks, so the plan's hanging points are real. The bath's scratch min of 8 was not reproduced in the built house: the built house has no lamp, and the hangers alone give 7.

waste.what: Testing candidate lamp layouts: I wrote a scratch apply script, copied build.nbt, set lamps into the copy, and re-ran mcd room once per layout (5 runs).
waste.cost: about 5 scratch runs and 1 helper script to get 4 numbers
waste.tool: mcd room --try 'x,y,z:lantern:hanging=false;...' (or a --lamps option on mcd light) to measure candidate lamp cells without copying the nbt

waste.what: Finding out why the lamp write was refused: I read build.mjs runParts and parts-report.json by hand to learn the shell's air claim is what blocks the room.
waste.tool: make.sh (or the room command) should print the lock's owner for each refused cell, e.g. 'refused: shell owns this air' with the owning part, so the diagnosis is one line

waste.what: Working out that the walk verdict NEEDS WORK came from a standable cell on top of the table lantern, not from a dark or unreachable floor.
waste.cost: 2 runs and reading the walk output by eye
waste.tool: mcd walk / mcd room should separate cells that are standable only on top of a placed object (lantern, slab) from unreached floor, so the verdict doesn't flag them

companions.task: Stop the masonry shell from writing air over the master bath interior (x65..68 z43..49 y11..16), so the room's furniture and lamp can be placed. The bath's 4 by 7 room is currently an owned air box.

Once the shell's air claim is lifted, place the bath's dressing table, tub, basin and barrels from the held layout in room-15.mjs, and confirm the table's standing lantern is not needed given the floor lantern.
